decisions.rationale: Gasoline flash-point recall is source-explicit and independently useful for Class-4 hazard comparison.
Gasoline water insolubility is a distinct substance-property proposition with practical extinguishing relevance.
Gasoline liquid relative density is distinct from vapor density and supports spill-behavior reasoning.
Gasoline vapor density versus air is independently testable and hazard-relevant.
Kerosene flash-point range is source-bound and materially contrasts with gasoline volatility.
Kerosene water insolubility is substance-specific and supports Class-4 handling distinctions.
Acetone flash point is a distinct numeric property with direct flammability relevance.
Acetone water solubility usefully contrasts with hydrocarbon liquids and is not a wording-only duplicate.
Ethanol flash point is an independent alcohol-property boundary.
Ethanol water miscibility tests a different property from flash point and has no canonical collision.
Methanol flash point is a source-explicit quantitative property distinct from ethanol and gasoline items.
Methanol vapor density tests air-relative vapor behavior and is distinct from liquid-density propositions.
Toluene flash point is independently useful for aromatic-liquid comparison.
Toluene liquid density correctly separates liquid density from vapor-density misconceptions.
Benzene flash point is source-explicit and tests a distinct aromatic flammability boundary.
Xylene vapor density is independently useful and not redundant with liquid-density questions.
Ethyl-acetate flash point is distinct from the existing canonical extinguishing-method question for the same substance.
Ethyl-acetate vapor density tests a separate physical property from flash point and extinguishing suitability.
Cross-substance flash-point ranking requires synthesis across registered properties rather than repeating a single recall.
Cross-substance water-solubility grouping is a synthesis decision and materially distinct from individual recalls.
Benzene liquid density is a separate property from benzene flash point and supports density comparison coverage.
Xylene flash point is distinct from its vapor-density item and source-explicit.
Ethyl-acetate liquid density is distinct from its vapor density and existing extinguishing question.
Diethyl-ether extreme flammability is label-backed, high-value Class-4 hazard knowledge with no collision.

collision_review.note: No B4 candidate materially collides with the 51 canonical questions or another accepted Wave 1 candidate. Same-substance items test distinct source-defined properties or synthesis decisions.
